name: Credit-cycle (Minsky) sector tilt via BankNifty relative strength
source: Hyman Minsky -- financial-instability hypothesis / credit-cycle-leads-real-economy (via Howard Marks' popularization of credit-cycle positioning)
construction: credit_scalar(t) = trend (3M and 6M EMA-of-return) of [BANKNIFTY return(t) - NIFTY500 return(t)], both from ../datasets/index_daily/banknifty.parquet and ../datasets/index_daily/nifty500.parquet (or macro_state.nifty500), causal (uses data <=t only). Cross-sectional score(date, name) = credit_scalar(t) if sector_map.macro_sector(name) in CREDIT-SENSITIVE set {Construction, Realty, Capital Goods, Automobile and Auto Components, Metals & Mining}, else -credit_scalar(t) if in DEFENSIVE set {Fast Moving Consumer Goods, Healthcare, Information Technology}, else 0. Join via data/universe/sector_map.parquet -> panel/panel_long.parquet (sector col already matches macro_sector categories, verified). Evaluate 1M and 1Y via shared harness.
expected_sign: + (credit-sensitive cyclicals outperform when BankNifty leads/expands; defensives outperform when BankNifty lags/contracts)
orthogonality_vs_7legs: Distinct axis from all 7 (EY, QMJ, PLAIN residual momentum, MA-65 slope, net-share-issuance, asset-growth, CFO/PAT) -- none use a banking-sector-specific leading indicator. Also distinct from wave4's own W4-09 (FX-beta rotation, uses USDINR not BankNifty) and W4-14 (bear-regime market-level SIZING classifier, does not use BankNifty at all). Must still gate corr<0.6 vs residual momentum before promotion (recent BankNifty winners could just be recent price winners) -- run the check, do not assume.
money_rationale: Bank credit availability is the classic Minsky leading indicator for capital-intensive/leveraged real-economy sectors (construction, capex, auto financing) -- the market re-prices credit-dependent cyclicals with a lag to bank-sector re-rating/de-rating. India's capex-cycle-in-progress narrative (already the firm's own 5Y growth thesis) makes this a directly monetizable, economically motivated tilt, not a data-mined correlation.
refinement_allowed: If the level/EMA construction is noisy: fall back to a discrete regime dummy (BankNifty 6M return percentile > 60th = credit-expanding, <40th = credit-contracting, else neutral) -- one child, same family ledger.
caveats: BankNifty daily history on disk is 2016-2026 only (~10yr, matches macro_state.parquet's window) -- no GFC-era coverage; treat as a regime-adjacent construction (fewer independent credit-cycle episodes than a pure cross-sectional factor), partially mitigated by scoring every name-date in the cross-section rather than a single market-level number per date.

name: Distress-composite (adapted Ohlson O-score / Campbell-Hilscher-Szilagyi style)
source: Ohlson (1980) O-score; Campbell-Hilscher-Szilagyi (2008) 'In Search of Distress Risk'; Dichev (1998) 'Is the Risk of Bankruptcy a Systematic Risk?' -- the distress-risk-puzzle literature (distressed firms have historically earned LOWER, not higher, returns)
construction: Adapted composite (literal Ohlson needs a current-asset/current-liability split MASTER_fundamentals_pit does not carry -- disclosed [INFERENCE] adaptation, not a fabricated formula). Per-date cross-sectional z-score rank-average (no fitted weights, per firm's own no-ML-combiner rule) of, all from data/fundamentals/MASTER_fundamentals_pit.parquet (long-format, metric_norm + available_date PIT join) + rnd/panel/panel_long.parquet: (1) leverage = total_liabilities/total_assets; (2) size = -mktcap_log; (3) profitability = net_profit/total_assets; (4) interest coverage = -operating_profit/interest (inverted: low coverage = high distress); (5) negative-equity dummy = 1 if (reserves + equity_capital) < 0; (6) earnings-deterioration dummy = 1 if net_profit declined for 2 consecutive fiscal years; (7) equity-vol proxy (Campbell-Hilscher's market-vol component) = vol_252 from panel_long. composite_distress = mean(z-scores of 1,2,4,5,6,7 with sign such that HIGH = more distressed; 3 entered as -z(profitability)). score = -composite_distress (LOW distress = high score). Evaluate 1Y/5Y via shared harness.
expected_sign: + for low-distress names (i.e. short/avoid high composite_distress)
data_assets: data/fundamentals/MASTER_fundamentals_pit.parquet (metrics: total liabilities, total assets, net profit, operating profit, interest, reserves, equity capital -- all confirmed present, verified via metric_norm value_counts)
orthogonality_vs_7legs: Distinct mechanism from all 7 -- this is a composite SOLVENCY/bankruptcy-probability score, not a single leverage or cash-quality leg. Nearest existing legs to gate against: CFO/PAT authenticity (both touch earnings quality but O-score is about balance-sheet fragility+size+equity-vol, not cash-vs-accrual divergence -- expect corr<0.5); net-share-issuance (distressed firms often issue equity for survival -- some overlap expected, gate <0.6); asset-growth (different economic story: overinvestment penalty vs balance-sheet fragility -- expect low corr). Also distinct from IDG-I-06 (deleveraging momentum, a single first-difference net-debt/EBITDA signal, already KILLED as a 'dead-cat not repair' pattern per CONSOLIDATION) -- this is a level composite, not a first-difference, and folds in size+coverage+earnings-trend+equity-vol that IDG-I-06 never touched.
money_rationale: The distress-risk anomaly is one of the most-replicated cross-market anomalies globally and is exactly the kind of mispricing the firm's own forensic red-flag gate (Beneish/Montier) is adjacent to but does not measure -- forensic gates catch MANIPULATION, not honest financial fragility. A firm can be un-manipulated and still be a bad bet because it is fragile. This gives the ranker a continuous distress dial that is complementary to (not redundant with) the forensic penalty block, and is especially relevant in the small/microcap tier where the firm already runs forensic gating.
refinement_allowed: If the 6-component composite is unstable/thin-coverage (interest and reserves have lower row-counts than core metrics per the schema scan): drop to a 4-component version (leverage, size, profitability, earnings-deterioration dummy) -- one child, same family ledger.
caveats: MASTER_fundamentals_pit is ~99% ANNUAL (verified, per rnd/IDEAS_GLOBAL.md) -- this is a level/trailing-annual construction, not a quarterly-refreshed distress signal (Campbell-Hilscher's original used monthly-updated market data blended with quarterly accounting; ours updates on the annual PIT cadence only, market-vol component (vol_252) is the only sub-monthly-refreshing piece).

name: Gold-vs-equity momentum as a Dalio-quadrant defensive/cyclical SECTOR tilt (cross-sectional selection, not exposure sizing)
source: Ray Dalio -- 'economic machine' / all-weather growth x inflation quadrants (adapted: true India CPI/growth/real-rate data is NOT on disk anywhere found -- see BLOCKED list -- so gold-vs-equity relative momentum, already a built macro_state.parquet column, is used as the best AVAILABLE on-disk proxy for a stagflation-fear / flight-to-real-assets regime, not a substitute for the real quadrant)
construction: regime_scalar(t) = sign of a 3M EMA of macro_state.parquet's gold_vs_equity_1m (goldbees return minus nifty500 return, already built, causal). Cross-sectional score(date, name) = regime_scalar(t) if sector_map.macro_sector(name) in REAL-ASSET/PRICING-POWER set {Metals & Mining, Oil Gas & Consumable Fuels, Fast Moving Consumer Goods}, else -regime_scalar(t) if in LONG-DURATION/GROWTH-MULTIPLE set {Information Technology, Consumer Services, Realty}, else 0. This is explicitly a WHICH-SECTORS-TO-OVERWEIGHT cross-sectional construction, not a WHICH-TOTAL-EXPOSURE-TO-CARRY sizing scalar.
expected_sign: + (real-asset/pricing-power sectors outperform long-duration growth sectors when gold is beating equity, i.e. stagflation-fear regime)
orthogonality_vs_7legs: Distinct axis from all 7 legs. IMPORTANT cross-reference for the merge/judge step: this SHARES A DATA FIELD (gold_vs_equity_1m) with wave4's own W4-14 (leading bear-regime classifier for SIZING), which uses gold_vs_equity_1m as one of several inputs into a market-level exposure-scalar logit. Do NOT treat this as a duplicate of W4-14 on that basis alone -- W4-14 answers 'how much total exposure', this answers 'which sectors within the cross-section'; but DO run an explicit correlation check between this factor's cross-sectional scores and W4-14's exposure scalar's implied tilts before promoting, since a real relationship there would mean this is partially just W4-14's information re-expressed at the sector level.
money_rationale: Dalio's core insight -- that different asset/sector baskets are the right holding in different growth x inflation regimes -- is a real, non-firm-owned mechanism (macro-regime-conditioned relative pricing power). We cannot build the TRUE quadrant (India CPI/growth data blocked) but the gold-vs-equity relationship is a well-documented real-asset-flight signal on its own and is already sitting unused as a plain scalar in macro_state.parquet -- turning it into a sector tilt (rather than only a market-level sizing input, its current sole use) extracts additional value from data already paid for and verified.
refinement_allowed: If the sector-dummy tilt is too coarse/noisy: restrict to the two cleanest legs only (Metals & Mining long vs Information Technology short) -- one child, same family ledger.
caveats: goldbees ETF data on disk starts 2021-01 (1,357 daily rows to 2026-07); macro_state's gold_vs_equity_1m column shows NaN in its earliest rows (pre-2018ish), so this factor's usable history is materially shorter than the other 7 legs' 21yr panel -- treat any standalone IC as a recent-era-only read, not a cross-regime-confirmed one.

name: Sector-level calendar seasonality (monsoon / festive / budget cycles) -- distinct from the already-dropped name-level version
source: Heston-Sadka cross-sectional return seasonality, re-scoped to SECTOR aggregation for India-specific structural calendar drivers (monsoon-linked rural demand, festive-season consumption/auto, Union Budget month policy-sector effects) -- not a new academic citation, a re-granularized construction of an idea the firm already tested at the wrong grain
construction: For each (macro_sector, calendar-month) pair: expanding-window (PIT, only years < current year -- no lookahead) mean of that sector's cross-sectional-average monthly return, computed from rnd/panel/panel_long.parquet grouped by sector+month. score(date, name) = the expanding historical same-calendar-month average return of name's sector at that date. Evaluate 1M horizon using the SAME event-time-safe lag-test methodology the firm already built for the name-level version (FRAMEWORK_CATALOG anti-overfit lesson #5: standard rebalance-lag test is mismatched for calendar factors).
expected_sign: + (sectors historically strong in the upcoming calendar month, on an expanding PIT basis, continue to be strong)
data_assets: rnd/panel/panel_long.parquet (sector, date, fwd_ret_1M_raw -- same panel already used for the name-level version)
orthogonality_vs_7legs: Distinct axis from all 7 legs (none touch calendar seasonality). MANDATORY pre-gate before this counts as a new bet at all: correlation vs the existing (already-tested, DROPPED-as-passenger-not-killed) name-level cross-sectional seasonality leg (IDG-G-10 / FINAL_MODEL 'Cross-sectional seasonality' card, IC_IR 0.44 standalone) MUST be checked first -- if corr>=0.6, this is just a lower-noise re-expression of an idea the firm already declined to keep (ΔIC_IR -0.047 as a composite passenger, 2x turnover), and should NOT be promoted regardless of its own standalone IC_IR. The distinguishing economic claim (aggregation cancels idiosyncratic noise, isolates genuine sector-structural calendar drivers) is only real if the correlation check confirms it.
money_rationale: India has genuine structural calendar drivers that operate at the SECTOR level (monsoon timing for agri-inputs/rural-FMCG, festive season for autos/consumer-durables/retail, Union Budget month for capex/infra/PSU-policy sectors) that a single stock's own noisy historical same-month return cannot cleanly isolate -- this is the cheapest possible test of whether the firm's prior seasonality kill-as-passenger was a signal-to-noise problem (fixable by aggregating) or a genuine absence of seasonal edge (not fixable by aggregating).
refinement_allowed: If the full 22-sector x 12-month grid is too sparse per cell in early panel years: restrict to the 6 sectors with the clearest India-specific calendar story (FMCG, Automobile and Auto Components, Capital Goods, Construction, Metals & Mining, Information Technology) -- one child, same family ledger.
caveats: The cheapest falsification here is NOT a full harness run -- it is the correlation check against the existing dropped name-level seasonality card's scores. Do that first (should take under 30 minutes) and only proceed to a full 1M harness evaluation if corr<0.6.
